subject: Proposal: phased reserved capacity with clawback windows and GPU-index price trigger
messages:
From: Beth Clarke <beth@veloxai.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity ask — looking for phased commit + price protection

Marcus,

Thanks again for the demo last week — team is excited about Aurora for our latency-critical agents. We’re trying to balance predictability and cost, and legal asked me to surface a couple of asks so procurement can model it: 

- Can Redwood support a phased reserved capacity commitment (start smaller, ramp over 6–12 months) rather than a single upfront slab?
- We’d like a GPU-index trigger: if spot/market GPU costs move >15% down, Velox should get automatic pass-through discount; if costs move up >20% we need a short notice renegotiation window.
- Clawback / usage true-up cadence: 90 vs 180 days? Which gives Redwood enough revenue visibility without hamstringing our growth plan.

Quick ask: can you send a sample term sheet and the decision/approval path at Redwood (who signs off on deeper discounts and indexation language)? We’re aiming to present an internal recommendation on Monday.

Appreciate it — Beth
Beth Clarke
Head of Platform Partnerships, Velox AI
beth@veloxai.com
+1 (415) 555-0189
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Beth Clarke <beth@veloxai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>; Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — looking for phased commit + price protection

Beth — thanks for laying out the asks. Attached is an initial proposal (phased-reserve-term-sheet-v1.pdf) that captures three configurable levers:

1) Phased ramp: 3 tranches (T0: 30% commit, T1 at month 4 -> additional 40%, T2 at month 8 -> remaining 30%). Each tranche recognized for billing/discount decisions once provisioned.
2) GPU-index trigger: we can include a market-index clause with asymmetric bands. Suggested: downward pass-through for >12% market price drop and a consult window for >22% increase (we prefer consult + short-term surcharge rather than unilateral renegotiation).
3) Clawback / true-up: default 120 days, with option to elect 90 days in exchange for a 0.75% higher discount tier.

High-level ask from our side: deeper-than-standard discounts (>=20%) for multi-year locked tranches require VP Finance approval; anything >=30% requires CRO sign-off. Karthik — can you confirm approval thresholds and whether finance can pre-approve a conditional 25% band for this deal?

Beth — attaching the v1 term sheet. If this shape looks reasonable I’ll run a sensitivity with Finance and loop in Legal for the index language.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
Attachment: phased-reserve-term-sheet-v1.pdf (application/pdf, 68KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — looking for phased commit + price protection

Marcus — I reviewed the v1 and ran a quick finance sensitivity (file: finance-sensitivity-20261212.xlsx). High level thoughts:

- Approvals: 20–25% effective discount can be approved by Finance Director (Monica); 25–35% requires VP Finance; >35% requires exec (CRO).
- Index band: the market index clause is workable, but we should avoid open-ended pass-throughs. I recommend a three-tier guard:
   * Downward market move >=12% -> automatic 50% of savings passed through (protects us for short-term volatility).
   * Downward >=25% -> full pass-through for the remainder of contract term.
   * Upward >=20% -> 60-day consult + temporary surcharge (capped at +10% until renegotiation).
- Cashflow impact: phased ramps reduce near-term revenue but improve conversion — we can offer a slightly higher discount on early tranches (T0) in exchange for an acceleration clause (if Velox hits usage milestones the discount extends to future tranches).

I’ve attached the sensitivity worksheet. Monica, can you confirm you can sign off up to 25%? If yes, Marcus can present a conditional 25% for initial tranche and flag the need for VP Finance for subsequent deep discounts.

Karthik
Finance, Redwood Inference
Attachment: finance-sensitivity-20261212.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask — looking for phased commit + price protection

Couple operational notes before we send to the customer: 

- Clawback window: I prefer 90 days if we can tie it to a usage milestone schedule (e.g., 75% of tranche capacity utilized for at least 30 of 90 days). That reduces churn risk and gives us a mechanics-based true-up.
- On the GPU-index: SRE & procurement prefer the consult + capped surcharge model for upward moves — it avoids sudden capacity rebalancing. We’ll need a fallback routing policy (auto-failover to on-demand at customer tier) and an SLO addendum (30-day increased support for ramp periods).
- Legal language: indexation needs a defined market source (we recommend the Redwood Composite GPU Spot Index — RCSI) and a monthly observation window (not instantaneous).

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deals/5327) — I’ll open a Docusign envelope for the v2 term sheet once we have Monica’s sign-off limit.

Grace
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Beth Clarke <beth@veloxai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>; Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>; Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>; Velox AI Legal <legal@veloxai.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Final: phased reserve term sheet v2 + next steps (DEAL-2026-5327)

Beth — thanks for the patience. Based on internal review we prepared a v2 term sheet (attached) that incorporates the following consensus items: 

- Phased ramp (30/40/30) over 8 months with tranche gating tied to provisioning and usage milestones.
- Clawback: default 120 days, optional 90 days if Velox elects the Milestone Protection schedule (75% utilization over 30/90 days).
- GPU-index: Redwood Composite GPU Spot Index (RCSI) used with a monthly observation window. Downward moves: >=12% -> 50% pass-through; >=25% -> full pass-through. Upward moves: >=20% -> 60-day consult window + temporary surcharge capped at +10% until formal renegotiation.
- Discount bands: up to 25% pre-approved by Finance Director; 25–35% requires VP Finance; >35% requires CRO sign-off. For deal modeling we can offer T0 at 18% and conditional extension to 22–25% if milestone triggers are met.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Velox to review v2 and confirm clawback preference (90 w/ milestone or 120 default).
2) If Velox accepts v2 shape, we’ll open a DocuSign envelope (link: https://docusign.com/Velox-DEAL-5327) for a Statement of Work + term sheet.
3) We’ll reserve the requested SKU pool for 30 days pending signature; final provisioning will follow once the first tranche invoice is paid.

Attachment: phased-reserve-term-sheet-v2.pdf (application/pdf, 72KB)

If you want a short call to walk through the index mechanics and approval path, I’m available Monday morning PST.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (650) 555-0133
